note: Discovery Map is a one-shot structured-JSON generator, not a conversational agent — every probe below is executionMode:'single-turn' (or 'background-scan' for DM-F04), with any 'prior state' a case needs (a pre-refinement tree, a supplied manual-capability list, evidence-tagged metrics) embedded directly as fixture data inside the probe action itself, rather than built up via run-tests.js's runMultiTurn()/dual-conversation orchestration. This is a deliberate compile-time choice, not an oversight: run-tests.js's runMultiTurn() snapshots state.draft before/after the probe (context.draftBefore/draftAfter) — a Requirement-Agent-specific property invoke-config.js's own state shape ({clientTraceId, lastTree}) doesn't have, so it would silently resolve to {} for Discovery Map. Baking fixed fixture data into the probe instead (e.g. DM-A01's `priorTree`) is also a materially stronger test than diffing against a second LLM call's own non-deterministic output would have been. probe.action mirrors invoke-config.js's real action contract exactly: {mode:'tree'|'tree-manual'|'dd'|'leak', ...}, never Requirement Agent's {content}. RESOLVED 2026-09-18 (was flagged here as an evaluator.js gap found during compile): evaluator.js's script_diff dispatch was hardcoded to Requirement-Agent-specific rubric keys and logic — fixed to dispatch generically via each agent's own scriptChecks.js; test-suite/agents/discovery-map/scriptChecks.js now implements all 11 script_diff rubric keys below (G, H1, A1-A4, F1-F4, L), verified against 26 pass/fail scenarios. All 19 v1-active cases now have a real evaluator path — the llm_judge-typed ones (H2, X, N) via evalLlmJudge(), the script_diff-typed ones via scriptChecks.js.
